The Halasur Police Station, Bengaluru filed this charge sheet against the accused persons for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323 R/w. Section 34 of IPC and Sec. 4 of D.P.Act.
2.

The brief facts of the prosecution case that:
That accused No.1 married C.W.1 on 11/08/2021 at Nagavelli Temple, KGF, Kolar District as per Hindu rituals.
After marriage CW1 was staying in her matrimonial home at House No. 199/A, 3rd Cross, 1st 'C' Main, Domlur Layout.
Accused No. 1 took and spent Rs. 50,000/- of CW1 for the wedding reception.

Thereafter, accused Nivedita.D vs Kiran on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97842286/
1 No. 1 transferred Rs. 25,000/- of CW1 to his account.

In this regard, when CW1 questioned accused No.1, he came home drunk and abused the CW1 in foul language,
subjected her to physical and mental cruelty by assaulting her with hands,
intentionally insulting C.W.1 and also by demanding for dowry from CW.1 and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323 R/w.
Section 34 of IPC and Sec. 4 of D.P.Act.
3.
The Investigating officer after completion of the investigation, filed the charge-sheet against the accused person.
This Court took cognizance for the said offence and registered the case and issued summons to the accused.
Accused appeared through his advocate and are enlarged on bail.
4. After compliance of Section 207 of Cr.P.C., this Court framed plea against the accused persons and read over the same to them in the language known to them.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Therefore, the case was posted for trial.
5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution got examined one witness as PW-1 and got marked two documents as per Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 and closed its side.
6. As the witness/victim turned hostile, the remaining witnesses were dropped and the statement of the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.

7. Heard the learned A.P.P. and learned counsel for the accused.
8.

The points that arise for my consideration are as under :-
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage of accused no.1 with CW1, all the accused persons subjected CW1 to physical and mental cruelty and assaulted her with hands, intentionally insulted her and demanded for dowry from CW.1 and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323 R/w Section 34 of IPC and Sec. 4 of D.P.Act ?
2. What order ?
9. My findings on the above said points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative.
 Point No.2 : As per the final order for  the following:
 REASONS 10. POINT No.1:-

It is the case of the prosecution that, the accused No.1 married C.W.1 on 11/08/2021, and after marriage CW1 was subjected to physical and mental cruelty for questioning the accused no.1 and CW1 was also abused in foul language and assaulted with hands.

It is also Nivedita.D vs Kiran on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97842286/
2 alleged that the accused demanded for dowry from CW.1 and thereby committed offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323 R/w Section 34 of IPC and Sec. 4 of D.P.Act.
11. CW1, the victim is examined as PW1.
She deposed that, she got married to accused No. 1 on 11/08/2022 and accused No. 2 and 3 are her father-in-law and mother-in-law.
After marriage she is residing in her matrimonial home.
She is leading a happy marital life.
CW.1 denied that the accused troubled her to bring dowry.
She denied that they abused her in foul language and assaulted her with hands.
She also deposed that she did not file any complaint against the accused persons in the police station.
Though PW1 identified her signatures on Ex.P1 and Ex.P2, she deposed that she does not know the contents of those documents.
Though she was treated as hostile by the prosecution nothing was elicited in her cross-examination.

12. On perusal, the prosecution had to prove that the accused physically and mentally harassed her,
abused her in foul language, assaulted her and demanded to bring dowry.
PW1 appeared before the Court and turned hostile.
She denied that the accused did not harass her in any way.
13. As the eye witness who is also the victim turned hostile, there is no iota of evidence to attract the offence alleged by the prosecution.
As such examination of the prosecution witnesses only for the purpose of completing the procedural aspect will not serve any judicious purpose and is sheer waste of the precious time of the Court.

At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and Another, (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."

entities.text: Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and Another, (1996) 9 SCC 766
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case is applicable to this case as well.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the Point No.1 is answered in the negative.

16. POINT No.2:- In view of my discussions on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
:O R D E R:
Acting under Section 255(1) of Cr.P.C., the Accused is acquitted for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323 R/w. Section 34 of IPC and Sec. 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond of the accused stands canceled.
Cash security to be refunded after three months.
